Effects of introductions on serendipity

1 Setup

The models use the cmdstanr backend, so CmdStan must be installed.

Code 
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(brms)
library(cmdstanr)
library(gt)
Code 
data <- readr::read_csv(here::here("data", "long_df_scored.csv"))

dir.create(here::here("models"), showWarnings = FALSE)
Code 
intro_labels <- c(
  no_introduction          = "No introduction",
  immersive_introduction   = "Immersive introduction",
  informative_introduction = "Informative introduction"
)

# All models share the same sampler settings.
# Fitted models are saved to models/ and only refitted when the data or formula change.
fit_brm <- function(formula, data, file_name) {
  brms::brm(
    formula = formula,
    data = data,
    family = brms::bernoulli(link = "logit"),
    backend = "cmdstanr",
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    iter = 2000,
    seed = 42,
    file = here::here("models", file_name),
    file_refit = "on_change"
  )
}

# Odds ratios with 95% credible intervals for the introduction terms
odds_ratios <- function(model, model_name) {
  brms::fixef(model) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Term") |>
    dplyr::filter(stringr::str_starts(Term, "intro")) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      Model     = model_name,
      Term      = unname(intro_labels[stringr::str_remove(Term, "^intro")]),
      OR        = exp(Estimate),
      Lower_CrI = exp(Q2.5),
      Upper_CrI = exp(Q97.5)
    )
}

# Proportion of ratings meeting each operationalization, per introduction type
prevalence_table <- function(df, vars, title, subtitle) {
  df |>
    dplyr::group_by(intro) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      n = dplyr::n(),
      dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(vars), mean),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(intro = unname(intro_labels[as.character(intro)])) |>
    gt::gt() |>
    gt::fmt_percent(columns = dplyr::all_of(vars), decimals = 1) |>
    gt::cols_label(intro = "Introduction type", n = "N") |>
    gt::cols_align(align = "left", columns = intro) |>
    gt::tab_header(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) |>
    gt::opt_table_lines(extent = "default")
}

1.1 Analysis subsets

TBS can only occur in the outside-preference condition, which contains the songs participants rated as unusual for them (se_1 ≥ 4). TDS can only occur in the within-preference condition, which contains the songs not rated as unusual (se_1 < 4). Each flavor is therefore analyzed on the ratings where it can occur, with no introduction as the reference category.

Code 
tbs_data <- data |>
  dplyr::filter(se_1 > 3) |>
  dplyr::mutate(intro = relevel(factor(intro), ref = "no_introduction"))

tds_data <- data |>
  dplyr::filter(se_1 < 4) |>
  dplyr::mutate(intro = relevel(factor(intro), ref = "no_introduction"))

c(tbs = nrow(tbs_data), tds = nrow(tds_data))
tbs tds 
821 535
Code 
dplyr::bind_rows(
  tbs = tbs_data,
  tds = tds_data,
  .id = "subset"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    subset = factor(
      subset,
      levels = c("tds", "tbs"),
      labels = c("Within-preference", "Outside-preference")
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::count(subset, intro) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = intro,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Total = rowSums(dplyr::across(-subset))) |>
  janitor::adorn_totals(where = "row") |>
  knitr::kable()

2.2 Main models (Table 5)

I fit multilevel Bayesian logistic regressions with crossed random intercepts for session (sess_id) and song (name). These models produce Table 5 of the paper.

Code 
m_tbs <- fit_brm(tbs ~ intro + (1 | sess_id) + (1 | name), tbs_data, "m_tbs")
m_tds <- fit_brm(tds ~ intro + (1 | sess_id) + (1 | name), tds_data, "m_tds")
Code 
dplyr::bind_rows(
  odds_ratios(m_tbs, "TBS (outside-preference)"),
  odds_ratios(m_tds, "TDS (within-preference)")
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Odds ratios with 95% credible intervals")
Loading required namespace: rstan
Odds ratios with 95% credible intervals
Model Term OR Lower_CrI Upper_CrI

TBS (outside-preference) Informative introduction 2.61 1.70 4.07
TDS (within-preference) Immersive introduction 3.23 1.87 5.83

2.3 Robustness checks

As a robustness check, I re-ran the models with alternative operationalizations (see the data preparation document). In all of them, only the surprise and unexpectedness items (se_3, se_4) qualify an experience as fortuitous. tds_no_uncover additionally drops the uncovering criterion (se_6, se_7).

Code 
m_tbs_fort_strict <- fit_brm(tbs_fort_strict ~ intro + (1 | sess_id) + (1 | name), tbs_data, "m_tbs_fort_strict")
m_tds_fort_strict <- fit_brm(tds_fort_strict ~ intro + (1 | sess_id) + (1 | name), tds_data, "m_tds_fort_strict")
m_tds_no_uncover  <- fit_brm(tds_no_uncover  ~ intro + (1 | sess_id) + (1 | name), tds_data, "m_tds_no_uncover")
Code 
dplyr::bind_rows(
  odds_ratios(m_tbs,             "TBS, main"),
  odds_ratios(m_tbs_fort_strict, "TBS, fortuitous without se_5"),
  odds_ratios(m_tds,             "TDS, main"),
  odds_ratios(m_tds_fort_strict, "TDS, fortuitous without se_5"),
  odds_ratios(m_tds_no_uncover,  "TDS, fortuitous without se_5, no uncovering")
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Odds ratios with 95% credible intervals across operationalizations")

3 Serendipity by song and introduction type

Each cell shows the rate with the number of ratings it is based on. Cells are small, so song-level differences should be read as descriptive.

Code 
song_heatmap <- function(df, outcome, title, subtitle) {
  df |>
    dplyr::group_by(genre, name, intro) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      n = dplyr::n(),
      count = sum(.data[[outcome]]),
      prop = mean(.data[[outcome]]),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(intro = factor(intro_labels[as.character(intro)], levels = intro_labels)) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = intro, y = name, fill = prop)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white") +
    geom_text(
      aes(
        label = paste0(scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1), "\n(", count, "/", n, ")"),
        color = ifelse(prop > 0.5, "white", "black")
      ),
      size = 2.5
    ) +
    scale_color_identity() +
    facet_grid(genre ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      name = paste(toupper(outcome), "rate"),
      labels = scales::percent,
      option = "magma",
      direction = -1,
      limits = c(0, 1)
    ) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA)
    )
}
Code 
song_heatmap(
  tbs_data, "tbs",
  title = "Taste-broadening serendipity rates by song",
  subtitle = "Outside-preference condition (se_1 ≥ 4)"
)
Code 
song_heatmap(
  tds_data, "tds",
  title = "Taste-deepening serendipity rates by song",
  subtitle = "Within-preference condition (se_1 < 4)"
)

4 Appendix: earlier TDS operationalization

The TDS rows of Table 3 in the originally submitted manuscript were estimated with an earlier operationalization that required the song to be within the listener’s typical preferences, interest, and uncovering, but not the fortuitous criterion described in Section 3.4. The model below reproduces those estimates for transparency; the corrected estimates are reported in Table 5 above.

Code 
tds_data_earlier <- tds_data |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    tds_uncover_only = as.integer(se_2 > 3 & (se_6 > 3 | se_7 > 3))
  )

m_tds_uncover_only <- fit_brm(
  tds_uncover_only ~ intro + (1 | sess_id) + (1 | name),
  tds_data_earlier,
  "m_tds_uncover_only"
)

odds_ratios(m_tds_uncover_only, "TDS, earlier operationalization (no fortuitous criterion)") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
Model Term OR Lower_CrI Upper_CrI
TDS, earlier operationalization (no fortuitous criterion) Immersive introduction 3.27 1.88 5.92
TDS, earlier operationalization (no fortuitous criterion) Informative introduction 9.94 5.19 20.11
